datasets.title: New Zealand: Copernicus Vegetation Index Anomaly (FAPAR Anomaly)
datasets.description: Fraction of Absorbed Photosynthetically Active Radiation (FAPAR) is a biophysical dimensionless quantity (its values range from 0/no absorption to 1/total absorption) used to assess the greenness and health of vegetation. FAPAR anomalies can be used as an indicator to detect and monitor the impacts of agricultural drought on the growth and productivity of vegetation. The data is presented in 10-day time composite of the Visible Infrared Imaging Radiometer Suite (VIIRS).. [Source: This metadata record was automatically extracted from the Humanitarian Data Exchange (HDX); Original dataset: https://data.humdata.org/dataset/nzl-anomalies-fapar-viirs]
datasets.details: Variations in the vegetation health and/or cover could be related to stress factors not related to droughts (e.g., plant diseases, pests, hail, flooding). To determine if changes in FAPAR are linked with a drought event or not, FAPAR data should be interpreted jointly with other indicators (as in the EDO Combined Drought Indicator).

lineage.description: FAPAR values from VIIRS satellite observations are composited at 10-day intervals and processed into anomalies by calculating the deviation from a long-term mean baseline (2012 to last available full year) at each grid cell to create a time series of agricultural drought indicators for New Zealand.

sources.name: European Commission, Joint Research Centre (JRC)
sources.description: Provides FAPAR biophysical measurements from VIIRS satellite radiometer suite processed into 10-day composites for vegetation monitoring

sources.name: Copernicus
sources.description: Copernicus Earth observation program providing satellite-derived vegetation and environmental monitoring data
